note: Extra deterministic practice items for Review vocabulary and collocation cards (Weeks 1–4). Used only for instant, no-AI extra practice; never alters review schedules.

items.prompt: It took him a few weeks to ___ to the new office.
items.reason: We say adapt to a new situation.

items.prompt: She ___ (adapt) quickly when she moved to Berlin.
items.reason: Past simple of adapt is adapted.

items.prompt: Starting that course was a ___ in my career.
items.reason: A turning point is a time when something important changes.

items.prompt: Meeting my business partner was a real ___ (2 words) in my life.
items.reason: We say a turning point in someone's life.

items.prompt: We ___ several challenges in our first year abroad.
items.reason: We say face a challenge.

items.prompt: Learning a language as an adult is a rewarding ___.
items.reason: A challenge is something new and difficult that needs effort.

items.prompt: I soon got used to ___ up early for work.
items.reason: After get used to, use the -ing form (not the infinitive).

items.prompt: It took me a month to ___ (get used to / drive) on the left.
items.reason: Use get used to + -ing for a new habit becoming normal.

items.prompt: When I ___ my university years, I smile.
items.reason: Look back on means think about something in the past.

items.prompt: We often look back ___ our first trip together.
items.reason: The multi-word verb is look back on.

items.prompt: I've never regretted ___ my old job.
items.reason: Use regret + -ing for something you did in the past.

items.prompt: She ___ (regret) not learning French at school.
items.reason: Regret takes -ing directly without of.

items.prompt: The city ___ began to feel like home.
items.reason: Gradually means slowly, a little at a time.

items.prompt: Her confidence ___ (gradual) grew over the year.
items.reason: Before the verb grew, use the adverb gradually.

items.prompt: Visiting Granada was a truly ___ trip.
items.reason: Memorable means easy to remember because it was special.

items.prompt: It was the most ___ (memory) evening of the holiday.
items.reason: Before the noun evening, use the adjective memorable.

items.prompt: She ___ a big decision to change career.
items.reason: We say make a decision, not do a decision.

items.prompt: Before you ___ (make) a big decision, talk to someone you trust.
items.reason: We say make a big decision.

items.prompt: Opening a small bookshop means ___ a risk.
items.reason: We say take a risk, not make or do a risk.

items.prompt: Are you willing to ___ (take) a risk and move abroad?
items.reason: We say take a risk.

items.prompt: It's never too late to ___ a change in your routine.
items.reason: We say make a change, not do a change.

items.prompt: They ___ (make) a few changes to the menu last week.
items.reason: Past simple of make is made: make a change.

items.prompt: I still ___ in touch with my college friends.
items.reason: We say keep in touch.

items.prompt: We've ___ (keep) in touch since we left university.
items.reason: Past participle of keep is kept: keep in touch.

items.prompt: You're ___ great progress with your English.
items.reason: We say make progress, not do progress.

items.prompt: He ___ (make) real progress after practising every day.
items.reason: We say make progress.

items.prompt: She ___ painting after she retired.
items.reason: Take up means start a new hobby or activity.

items.prompt: I want to ___ (take up) swimming this autumn.
items.reason: Use take up for starting a new activity.

items.prompt: His main ___ is to open a small bakery.
items.reason: An ambition is something you really want to do in life.

items.prompt: She has always had the ___ (ambitious) to run a marathon.
items.reason: After the, use the noun ambition.

items.prompt: Our ___ is to finish the house before winter.
items.reason: A goal is something you want to do and plan for.

items.prompt: Write down one realistic ___ (1 word) for this month.
items.reason: We say a realistic goal.

items.prompt: If you practise every day, you'll ___ your goal.
items.reason: We say achieve a goal.

items.prompt: She worked hard and ___ (achieve) top marks in the exam.
items.reason: Past simple of achieve is achieved.

items.prompt: We ___ to move closer to the coast next year.
items.reason: Intend means plan. Careful! Spanish pretender means intend, but English pretend means fingir.

items.prompt: I ___ (intend) to finish this book before Sunday.
items.reason: Use intend to + verb for a plan.

items.prompt: She built a successful ___ in nursing.
items.reason: Career is your working life; a university course is a degree.

items.prompt: He decided to change ___ (1 word) and become a teacher.
items.reason: We say change career.

items.prompt: The ___ for sending the form is Friday at 5 p.m.
items.reason: A deadline is the last day or time you can do something.

items.prompt: We have a tight ___ (1 word), so let's start today.
items.reason: We say a tight deadline.

items.prompt: He's going to apply ___ a job at the library.
items.reason: We say apply for a job or course.

items.prompt: Over forty people ___ (apply) for the position last week.
items.reason: Past simple of apply is applied: apply for a position.

items.prompt: I'm really looking forward to ___ you on Saturday.
items.reason: After look forward to, use the -ing form.

items.prompt: She's looking forward ___ (to / start) her new course.
items.reason: Look forward to is followed by -ing.

items.prompt: She's ___ to pass her driving test this year.
items.reason: Determined means very sure you will do something even if it's hard.

items.prompt: He was ___ (determine) to finish the race.
items.reason: Use the adjective determined + to + verb.

items.prompt: I'm working ___ a B2 certificate this year.
items.reason: We say work towards a goal or qualification.

items.prompt: She's ___ (work towards) a degree in design.
items.reason: Use work towards for steady effort toward a goal.

items.prompt: Calling the college is ___ the first step.
items.reason: We say take the first step, not give the first step.

items.prompt: I'll ___ (take) the first step and update my CV tonight.
items.reason: We say take the first step.

items.prompt: This workshop will help you ___ your skills.
items.reason: We say improve your skills.

items.prompt: Practising aloud is a great way to ___ (improve) your speaking skills.
items.reason: We say improve your skills.

items.prompt: I keep ___ off calling the dentist.
items.reason: Put off means delay doing something.

items.prompt: Don't put ___ off until tomorrow — do it now.
items.reason: With a pronoun, put it between put and off: put it off.

items.prompt: It helps to ___ a clear goal at the start of the month.
items.reason: We say set a goal.

items.prompt: I've ___ (set) myself a goal of walking every morning.
items.reason: Set has the same past participle: set yourself a goal.

items.prompt: We worked late on Thursday to ___ the deadline.
items.reason: We say meet a deadline, not complete a deadline.

items.prompt: She always ___ (meet) her deadlines on time.
items.reason: We say meet a deadline.

items.prompt: The new café has been a huge ___.
items.reason: After a huge, we need the noun success.

items.prompt: If you keep trying, you'll ___ (success) in the end.
items.reason: After you'll, we need the verb succeed.

items.prompt: She ___ really well with her new flatmates.
items.reason: Get on with means have a friendly relationship with someone.

items.prompt: Do you get on ___ your neighbours?
items.reason: The full phrase is get on with someone.

items.prompt: Let's meet for coffee on Friday and ___.
items.reason: Catch up means meet and share your latest news.

items.prompt: It was lovely to ___ (catch up) with Marta after the summer.
items.reason: We say catch up with someone.

items.prompt: We should ___ a time to meet next week.
items.reason: Arrange means plan or organise (Spanish arreglar a bike is fix).

items.prompt: I've ___ (arrange) to meet Ana outside the café.
items.reason: We say arrange to do something.

items.prompt: Try to stick to a ___ during busy weeks.
items.reason: We say stick to a routine.

items.prompt: A short walk is part of my daily ___ (1 word).
items.reason: We say daily routine.

items.prompt: You can always rely ___ David to help.
items.reason: We say rely on someone, not rely in.

items.prompt: She's very ___ (rely) — she never forgets a promise.
items.reason: Reliable is the adjective from rely on.

items.prompt: Let's talk and clear up this ___.
items.reason: We say clear up a misunderstanding.

items.prompt: It was just a silly ___ (understand) about the time.
items.reason: A misunderstanding is when someone gets the wrong idea.

items.prompt: Can I invite some friends ___ on Saturday?
items.reason: In British English we say invite someone round to your home.

items.prompt: They ___ (invite) us round for dinner last Friday.
items.reason: We say invite someone round.

items.prompt: There was an ___ silence when nobody spoke.
items.reason: Awkward describes an uncomfortable or embarrassing social moment.

items.prompt: It was an ___ (1 word) situation, but we laughed about it later.
items.reason: We say an awkward situation.

items.prompt: He ___ asked if we could turn the music down.
items.reason: Politely means in a respectful, kind way.

items.prompt: You can always disagree ___ (polite).
items.reason: After the verb disagree, use the adverb politely.

items.prompt: She always ___ an effort to learn her neighbours' names.
items.reason: We say make an effort, not do an effort.

items.prompt: We should ___ (make) an effort to keep the kitchen tidy.
items.reason: We say make an effort.

items.prompt: We ___ a lot in common: we both love hiking.
items.reason: We say have a lot in common.

items.prompt: My flatmate and I have a lot in ___ (1 word).
items.reason: The expression is have a lot in common.

items.prompt: Please ___ in touch if your train is late.
items.reason: We say get in touch, not put in touch.

items.prompt: I'll ___ (get) in touch with the landlord tomorrow.
items.reason: Get in touch means contact someone.

items.prompt: Why don't you ___ for dinner on Sunday?
items.reason: Come over means visit someone at their home.

items.prompt: My sister ___ (come over) for coffee yesterday afternoon.
items.reason: Past simple of come over is came over.

items.prompt: He always ___ his promises.
items.reason: We say keep a promise, not complete a promise.

items.prompt: It's important to ___ (keep) a promise to a friend.
items.reason: We say keep a promise.

items.prompt: I'll ___ later to return your book.
items.reason: Pop round is informal British English for a short visit.

items.prompt: Feel free to pop ___ (1 word) for a cup of tea.
items.reason: The phrasal verb is pop round.

items.prompt: A good ___ lasts for many years.
items.reason: After a good, we need the noun friendship.

items.prompt: Nobody smiled at us; the receptionist seemed quite ___ (friend).
items.reason: Unfriendly is the negative adjective.

items.prompt: Eating twelve grapes at midnight is a famous Spanish ___.
items.reason: A tradition is something people have done for a long time.

items.prompt: Visitors love trying ___ (tradition) dishes in the old town.
items.reason: Before the noun dishes, use the adjective traditional.

items.prompt: Taking off your shoes indoors is a local ___.
items.reason: Custom (singular) means a local habit; customs (with -s) is at the airport.

items.prompt: The guide explained an old ___ (1 word) from the region.
items.reason: A custom is a usual way of doing things in a place.

items.prompt: Bath is a popular ___ for a weekend away.
items.reason: A destination is a place people travel to.

items.prompt: We finally reached our ___ (1 word) at midnight.
items.reason: We say reach your destination.

items.prompt: We ___ early to avoid the traffic.
items.reason: Set off means start a journey.

items.prompt: What time are you going to set ___ (1 word) tomorrow?
items.reason: The phrasal verb is set off.

items.prompt: It's easy to ___ the city by tram.
items.reason: Get around means travel from place to place in a town or area.

items.prompt: We rented bikes to ___ (get around) the island.
items.reason: We say get around a city or island.

items.prompt: We were ___ with the bus ticket machine.
items.reason: We say unfamiliar with something you don't know.

items.prompt: She felt nervous in an ___ (familiar) part of town.
items.reason: Unfamiliar means new and not known to you.

items.prompt: The guesthouse had a warm, ___ atmosphere.
items.reason: Welcoming means friendly and making visitors feel at home.

items.prompt: Everyone in the village was really ___ (welcome) to visitors.
items.reason: Use the adjective welcoming.

items.prompt: Ask a ___ baker for the freshest bread.
items.reason: Local means from the nearby area.

items.prompt: Fresh ___ (1 word) fruit is sold at the market every Sunday.
items.reason: We say local fruit or local food.

items.prompt: We ___ a guided tour of the Roman Baths.
items.reason: We say take a guided tour, not make a guided tour.

items.prompt: I'd love to ___ (take) a guided tour of the castle.
items.reason: We say take a guided tour.

items.prompt: Don't leave without ___ the local food.
items.reason: We say try the local food, not prove the local food.

items.prompt: We always ___ (try) the local food when we visit a new place.
items.reason: We say try the local food.

items.prompt: For a weekend trip, it's easier to ___ light.
items.reason: Travel light means take very little luggage.

items.prompt: We only took small backpacks so we could travel ___ (1 word).
items.reason: The collocation is travel light.

items.prompt: We decided to ___ overnight in York.
items.reason: Stop overnight means stay one night during a journey.

items.prompt: They ___ (stop) overnight at a hotel near the ferry port.
items.reason: Past simple of stop is stopped: stop overnight.

items.prompt: Because the train was delayed, we ___ our connection.
items.reason: We say miss a connection, not lose a connection.

items.prompt: Hurry up or we'll ___ (miss) our connection in Madrid.
items.reason: We say miss a connection.

items.prompt: It's a long drive, so let's ___ our journey in Zaragoza.
items.reason: Break your journey means stop partway through a long trip.

items.prompt: We ___ (break) our journey with an overnight stay in York.
items.reason: Past simple of break is broke: break your journey.

items.prompt: The city is famous for its lively ___ events.
items.reason: Before the noun events, use the adjective cultural.

items.prompt: Travelling helps you learn about another ___ (1 word).
items.reason: After another, use the noun culture.
